questions.question: What is the difference between GET and POST requests?
questions.answer:
Short answer: GET reads data: parameters go in the URL, it should not change anything on the server, and it can be cached and bookmarked. POST sends data in the request body to create something or trigger an action; it is not idempotent and is not cached by default.

How it works:
GET: data in the query string, like /api/questions?topic=closures; read with req.query
POST: data in the body (JSON or form); read with req.body after express.json()
Safe and idempotent: repeating a GET changes nothing; repeating a POST can create two records
Caching and history: browsers and CDNs cache GET; POST stays out of the URL, history and most logs

Example: GET /api/questions?topic=closures lists questions. POST /api/auth/login sends the email and password in the body.

Common mistake: Saying POST is "secure" because the data is not in the URL. Without HTTPS both are plain text on the network.

Interview tip: Mention the other methods: PUT replaces, PATCH updates part of a resource and DELETE removes; PUT and DELETE are idempotent too.
